records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do up to **18 months** of Academic Training (AT), or the length of their degree program if that's shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. [ISSS's AT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment) doesn't give the details of that extension, so ask an ISSS advisor.

Other time rules from that page:
- AT done while studying and AT done after your program ends are added together.
- Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- The total training period can't exceed the length of your academic program.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- Submit your request to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends allowing about three weeks for processing.

**Duration of status:** DHS published a final rule eliminating "duration of status" on July 17, 2026. It would have taken effect September 15, but a [September 14, 2026 court order](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) postponed it and barred DHS from implementing it. ISSS is monitoring the situation. If you're planning post-completion AT, confirm the current rules with an ISSS advisor.
